summary: An announcement from BBN with two items of network news. The first and main one is that the new IMP software, described in RFCs 331, 343 and 359, was released on July 18, 1972 and ran with few problems. BBN asks users to be patient and to report bugs.

plainLanguage.summary: BBN reported that new IMP software had been released and ran with few problems during its first period of operation. The notice also describes a TIP issue, asks users to report faults and explains that site power failures were causing outages.

subtitle: A release update on IMP software and site power problems

tldr.problem: BBN was introducing new IMP software while network sites were also experiencing outages caused by local power and cooling problems.
tldr.mechanism: The notice reports the software release, describes a known TIP allocation issue and summarizes recent site power failures.
tldr.outcome: BBN asked users to report suspected malfunctions and sites to check specified switches on Model 516 IMPs.

today: RFC 374 is an operational update about an IMP software release and power-related outages. It also records a known TIP allocation problem under investigation at the time.

sections.title: New IMP Software Released
sections.content:
BBN says the new IMP software was released on July 18 and ran until Wednesday afternoon with very few problems attributed to the new system. BBN expected to leave it running permanently, while warning that bugs could still appear.

The notice asks users to report suspected network malfunctions to the Network Control Center promptly, even if they are not certain of the cause.
sections.plainLanguage: The new IMP software had run with few reported problems, and BBN planned to keep it in use. Users were asked to report anything that might be a malfunction.

sections.title: A Known TIP Allocation Problem
sections.content:
BBN reports that the new system worsened a long-standing TIP problem: a TIP might fail to send an Allocate control message for an active connection. This could block the path from a server to a user. The problem appeared more likely with several users and a TENEX server, based on the data available to BBN.

BBN says work on the problem had high priority and asks users to report other cases.
sections.plainLanguage: A TIP could fail to send a control message needed for a server to send data to a user. BBN was investigating and asked sites to report when it happened.

sections.title: Power Failures at Network Sites
sections.content:
The second part of the notice describes power-related outages. BBN says that between one-quarter and one-half of IMP downtime in June came from site power failure. It also recounts air-conditioning failures at two sites over a July weekend and a transformer failure that took IMP 27 out of action for several hours.

The notice says the NCC or site staff had little ability to restore service in these cases and expected such problems to continue during the summer.
sections.plainLanguage: Local power and cooling failures had taken network equipment offline. The notice explains that these outages were difficult for the network center to fix.
